flashcard_questions.q: What is weathering in coastal geography?
flashcard_questions.a: The breakdown of rock in its original place by physical, chemical or biological processes.

flashcard_questions.q: What is freeze–thaw weathering in rock?
flashcard_questions.a: Repeated freezing and expansion of water in cracks that shatters the rock.

flashcard_questions.q: By how much does water expand when it freezes inside a crack in rock?
Why is rainwater naturally slightly acidic?
flashcard_questions.a: It absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to limestone when the weak acid in rainwater reacts with it?
What is mass movement at the coast?
flashcard_questions.a: The downhill movement of material under the force of gravity.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of mass movement leaves a scree slope at the cliff base?
Which type of mass movement rotates a saturated cliff section along a curved surface?
flashcard_questions.a: Slumping, also known as rotational slip.

flashcard_questions.q: What is fetch in relation to waves?
flashcard_questions.a: The distance of open water over which the wind blows to create waves.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do constructive waves build up a beach?
flashcard_questions.a: Their strong swash deposits more material than their weak backwash removes.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do destructive waves strip material from a beach?
flashcard_questions.a: Their strong backwash drags away more material than their weak swash deposits.

flashcard_questions.q: Which erosion process compresses air inside cracks until the rock breaks away?
Which erosion process hurls pebbles at the cliff face like sandpaper?
Which erosion process makes rocks smaller and rounder as they collide?
What is longshore drift at the coast?
flashcard_questions.a: The zigzag movement of sediment along a coastline caused by waves arriving at an angle.

notes: 15 cards: 5 term-to-definition (weathering, freeze–thaw, mass movement, fetch, longshore drift), 3 process-to-effect naming the process (hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition), 2 mass-movement identification cards (rockfall, slumping), 2 cause-to-consequence on wave type (constructive, destructive), 2 chemical weathering cause cards, 1 figure card (9% expansion). No case study appears in this lesson, so no case-study cards. Solution as an erosion process, the four transport methods and the UK prevailing-wind direction were trimmed to stay within 15 and to stop four near-identical process answers interfering.
